jobs.title: Director of Grants, Contracts & Financial Compliance
jobs.description:
About Glide

GLIDE is a nationally recognized center for social justice, dedicated to fighting systemic injustices, creating pathways out of poverty and crisis, and transforming lives. Through its integrated comprehensive services, advocacy initiatives, and inclusive community, GLIDE empowers individuals, families, and children to achieve stability and to thrive. GLIDE is on the forefront of addressing some of society’s most pressing issues, including poverty, housing and homelessness, and racial and social justice. GLIDE’s mission is to create a radically inclusive, just, and loving community mobilized to alleviate suffering and break the cycles of poverty and marginalization.

Position Summary

The Director of Grants, Contracts & Financial Compliance (internally known as the Director of Grants & Contracts) provides strategic leadership and oversight of the organization's government contracts, grants, and restricted funding portfolio, including financial compliance, contract billing, reimbursement processes, budget oversight, and fiscal risk management. This position is responsible for ensuring compliance with all federal, state, local, and private funding requirements while maximizing reimbursement, minimizing organizational risk, and supporting program success.

The position involves driving important financial and operational insights with senior leaders and requires strong management skills. They will mentor and manage the contract team to provide strong Programs, Development, Finance, and Accounting partnerships. The ideal candidate will have a deep background in government-funded financial management, grants and contracts administration, financial compliance, and general business analysis, with demonstrated experience managing teams and collaborating across functions.

Essential Duties And Operational Responsibilities

Strategic Advice and Partnership

Develop and implement the organization's contracts and grants administration strategy.
Establish policies, procedures, and internal controls governing contract and grant management.
Provide leadership on compliance with federal Uniform Guidance, state regulations, City and County contracting requirements, and private foundation requirements.
Advise executive leadership regarding contractual risk, compliance issues, and operational impacts.
Lead continuous improvement initiatives to streamline contract administration, billing, reporting, and compliance processes.
Build collaborative partnerships across Programs, Development, Finance, Accounting, and Executive Leadership to ensure successful funding implementation.
Translate complex funding requirements into practical operational guidance.
Serve as the organization's subject matter expert on grants and contract administration.

Contract Administration

Oversee the financial administration of all government contracts and grant agreements from award through closeout.
Develop strategies to maximize contract reimbursement and recoverable revenue while ensuring compliance with funding requirements.
Identify opportunities to improve revenue capture through contract amendments, budget modifications, and funding reallocations.
Partner with program leadership to optimize utilization of awarded funding.
In collaboration with program teams, monitor contract performance, deliverables, budgets, amendments, and renewal timelines.
Maintain centralized contract records and document management systems.
Coordinate subcontract agreements and monitor subrecipient compliance.
Develop monitoring systems for contract compliance and conduct periodic internal control reviews.
Ensure required supporting documentation is maintained for all expenditures. Monitor regulatory changes affecting funding.

Audit and Financial Management

Oversee preparation and monitoring of contract and grant budgets.
Ensure accurate billing, reimbursement requests, and revenue recognition.
Monitor spending against awarded budgets and identify potential funding risks.
Work closely with accounting team on month-end and year-end reporting.
Oversee indirect cost calculations, cost allocations, and allowable cost determinations.
Serve as the primary Finance lead for contract and grant related audits, monitoring visits, and funder reviews.
Coordinate responses to federal, state, city, and private funder audit requests.
Develop and monitor corrective action plans related to grant compliance findings.
Develop multi-year revenue forecasts for government contracts and grants.
Monitor funding trends and expiration timelines to identify future financial risks and opportunities.
Provide executive leadership with regular forecasting and portfolio analysis.

Minimum Qualifications

BA/BS degree in relevant field and 10+ years of progressively responsible experience in nonprofit grants management, government contracts, finance, or accounting.
Minimum 5 years leading and supervising grants and contracts teams.
Experience managing a complex portfolio of federal, state, county, city, and foundation funding.
Experience supporting organizations with annual operating budgets exceeding $25 million preferred.
Experience launching and leading strategic initiatives at a multi-service agency.
Experience working in a community-based social service agency with adults and families in relationship to homelessness and poverty and the problems that often come alongside these experiences.
Federal Uniform Guidance (2 CFR Part 200).
Single Audit requirements.
GAAP
Cost allocation methodologies.
Indirect cost rate calculations.
Government reimbursement methodologies.
Restricted fund accounting.
Contract lifecycle management.

Physical Requirements

Ability to work on a computer and see details of objects at close range.  
Ability to hear within normal range, and communicate effectively (in person, telephone or Zoom ).  
Finger dexterity and the ability to use all standard office equipment.  
Sit or stand comfortably; and the ability to navigate throughout office spaces (via elevator or stairs).

$140,000 - $150,000 a year

This is a fulltime (40 hours/week), Exempt position.

Work Environment

GLIDE’s buildings are located in the Tenderloin neighborhood.  GLIDE maintains an "open door" policy to the community and its clients, who frequently enter and leave the building.

About the Organization:
Compass Family Services is a 100+ year old nonprofit working on the front lines of San Francisco’s homeless crisis. We provide families experiencing or at risk of homelessness with comprehensive support to address immediate needs and ensure long-term success.

About the team:
Compass Urgent Accommodation Voucher program provides temporary emergency hotel rooms for families and pregnant people in crisis. In addition to a hotel room, the program helps families connect with services and a path to stable housing.

Schedule: Sunday - Thursday, 1-9 pm

Compensation:
70,000 - 80,000 annually

Location:
1254 Market St., San Francisco and at the hotel sites. Fully in-person.

Organizational Core Competencies:
Accountable / Adaptable / Client-centered / Collaborative / Committed to Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging / Resourceful

Role Description:
The Assistant Program Director works with Program Director to oversee the day to day services of CUAV program and respond to emergency situations when they arise. This includes supervision of CUAV Staff, administrative and program design and implementation, as well as providing direct support to clients. The Assistant Director will work across multiple sites to support the needs of clients and staff.

Specific Responsibilities Include

Supervise and support case managers and other staff, including: hiring, training, scheduling, stepping in with tough client situations or lapses in coverage, supporting professional development, and evaluating performance.
Implement program policies equitably; de escalate and appropriately follow-up with clients when needed.
Build and cultivate collaborative community partnerships, including with funders.
Strengthen partnership and effective communication with partnership hotels and staff; respectfully advocate on behalf of clients and staff when necessary.
Assist with coordinating intakes, transfers and discharges
Represent the CUAV program in both internal and external meetings; offer shelter perspective on behalf of shelter clients and shelter staff.
Manage the CUAV program, in partnership with the Day Shift Assistant Program Director,in the absence of the Program Director

Qualifications

Minimum 3 years relevant experience in social work or a related field required
Deep understanding of issues facing homeless and low-income families.
Experience with deescalation and working with people in crisis.
Strong interpersonal, listening and communication skills
Outstanding work habits: organized, reliable, team-oriented
Ability to work independently as well as to inspire and lead a committed team
Strong computer skills with proficiency in Microsoft Programs (Outlook, Word, Excel, Power Point, etc.) and Zoom. Salesforce experience a plus.
Deep commitment to and demonstrated success discussing, integrating, and promoting diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging throughout a complex and dynamic organization.
Previous supervisory experience is strongly preferred
Spanish is not required for the role, but extremely helpful. Candidates who speak fluent Spanish are especially encouraged to apply.

Salary range: $70,000 - $80,000 depending on experience. Exempt (salaried) role.
Paid time off: 4 weeks of vacation your first year, increasing to 5 in your second. Also paid holidays, sick time, family leave.
Insurance: health, dental and vision insurance are fully covered by Compass for employees and dependent children. We also provide long term disability and life insurance.

Hackensack Meridian Health
is seeking an experienced, visionary, and passionate Family Medicine leader to become the new Residency Program Director as well as the Medical Director of the teaching practice at JFK University Medical Center. This is an outstanding leadership opportunity for a dedicated physician committed to academic excellence, clinical innovation, and the training of the next generation of Family Medicine physicians.

The Program Director will provide strategic and operational leadership for the Family Medicine Residency Program, ensuring full compliance with ACGME and institutional requirements. This role is responsible for cultivating a supportive and academically rigorous learning environment, fostering faculty development, and ensuring the continued success of the program. As Medical Director of the Family Medicine Center, the selected physician will oversee day-to-day clinical operations, quality and safety initiatives, and patient care processes aligned with Joint Commission and NCQA Patient-Centered Medical Home standards. The Medical Director will serve as a role model for compassionate, evidence-based care, and an advocate for both patients and staff.

Provide strategic leadership and direction for the Family Medicine Residency Program in collaboration with department and institutional leadership.
Oversee the design, implementation, and evaluation of the residency curriculum, ensuring alignment with ACGME milestones and competencies.

Ensure continuous program improvement through data-driven assessment, scholarly activity, and adherence to accreditation standards.
Direct and support quality improvement initiatives to enhance patient outcomes, safety, and satisfaction.
Maintain clinical engagement (approximately 20% clinical time) providing high-quality, patient-centered care within the Family Medicine Center.
Oversee compliance with institutional, state, and federal regulations related to residency education and clinical operations.
Collaborate with health system leadership on strategic planning, budgeting, and staff development initiatives.
Promote diversity, equity, and inclusion within the residency program and clinical environment.

Qualifications:

MD or DO degree with Board Certification in Family Medicine (ABFM or AOA).
Minimum of 5 years of progressive leadership experience in graduate medical education and clinical practice.
Demonstrated expertise in curriculum development, faculty mentorship, and quality improvement initiatives.
Proven ability to lead and inspire teams, manage complex academic programs, and drive innovation in medical education.
Excellent communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills.
Eligibility for medical licensure in New Jersey.

Deputy Executive Director of Operations - Exceptional Student Education

Position Summary

The Deputy Executive Director of Exceptional Student Education (ESE) serves as a key member of the ESE executive leadership team and supports the Senior Executive Director in providing strategic and operational leadership across the division. This position provides oversight for assigned ESE departments, programs, leaders, and strategic initiatives, ensuring effective implementation of District priorities and compliance with applicable federal and state special education requirements.

The Deputy Executive Director leads efforts related to operational effectiveness, staffing, professional learning, program implementation, compliance initiatives, and continuous improvement. Working collaboratively with ESE leadership, school administrators, Human Resources, Finance, Operations, and other District departments, the position establishes systems of accountability, monitors progress toward division goals, resolves barriers impacting schools and families, and supports high-quality services and outcomes for students with disabilities.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree required. Master's Degree strongly preferred (Educational Leadership, Special Education, Public Administration, or a related field preferred).
Minimum of five (5) years of professional experience, including a minimum of three (3) years of supervisory experience and experience leading operations at scale. Preference for administrative experience in public education.
Demonstrated experience designing, building, and implementing organization-wide systems, processes, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Demonstrated experience leading recruitment and staffing, professional learning (including paraprofessional training), parent and family engagement, and constituent response.
Demonstrated experience developing, tracking, and reporting Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) or Objectives and Key Results (OKRs) and using data to drive decision-making.
Strong organizational skills and the ability to model effective organizational systems for others.
Excellent interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills, and strong customer service skills.

Essential Functions

Systems & Continuous Improvement

Provide executive leadership and oversight for all ESE operations, ensuring the organization runs smoothly and strategically.
Design, build, and continuously improve systems, structures, and processes across all of ESE to strengthen the quality, consistency, and efficiency of work organization wide.
Develop, refine, and implement operations policies, administrative guidelines, and manuals; ensure adherence and recommend improvements as needed.

People & Talent

Lead ESE staff recruitment and staffing strategy in partnership with the Office of Human Resources; oversee job postings, hiring processes, and onboarding to ensure ESE is fully and appropriately staffed.
Oversee the development and delivery of paraprofessional (para) training and professional learning; monitor completion and effectiveness and adjust based on data.
Supervise, coach, and evaluate operational directors, supervisors, and staff; build and sustain a high-performing operations team.

Family & Constituent Engagement

Lead ESE parent and family engagement strategy and initiatives to strengthen partnerships between families and the District.
Direct the constituent response system and serve as a senior point of escalation for constituent questions and concerns, ensuring timely, high-quality resolution.
Oversee internal communication with all ESE staff, ensuring information is shared clearly, consistently, and in a timely manner across the organization.

Data, Systems & Accountability

Provide management-level oversight of ESE Information Systems and student data, including Medicaid billing, student placement, and the administration of PowerSchool Special Programs, ensuring accuracy, integrity, security, and compliance.
Establish, track, and report Key Performance Indicators (KPIs); analyze operational data and produce reports for ESE and District leadership that conspicuously identify problem areas and drive continuous improvement.

Operational Oversight & Support

Oversee operational support for enrollment, facilities, field trips, special events, Special Olympics, and ESE technology, as applicable.
Support the ESE department with the development and execution of crisis management plans; assist on-site and remotely in the event of a crisis.
Ensure documented policies and guidelines related to investigations of alleged student misconduct, staff misconduct, or Title IX matters are followed; liaise with relevant central office departments when necessary.
Collaborate with and support ESE central office and school-level administrators to manage and resolve conflict among constituents in a timely manner.
Proactively and consistently communicate with the Senior Executive Director and ESE Lead Administrators regarding operational matters requiring immediate follow-up.
Perform other duties as assigned by the Senior Executive Director or designee.

jobs.description:
The University of Virginia’s College at Wise is accepting applications for a Program Director.

The Program Director directs the operations of the GO Virginia Region One Council. As the support organization for the Commonwealth’s GO Virginia program, UVA Wise Office of Strategic Engagement and Government Relations is responsible for supporting the work of the Region One Council, which includes the implementation of the Growth and Diversification Plan, grants management, constituent relations and adherence to the freedom of information act regulations. This position is responsible for the coordination, direction, and implementation of the council activities in the thirteen county/three-city region and assists in the management of the annual budget preparation and program review. Partnerships formed to support these efforts are diverse: representing government, education, industry, non-profits, entrepreneurs, chambers of commerce, and private foundations. Operating since 2017, GO Virginia is a statewide program. This position is fully grant funded and focuses on the Southwestern region of the Commonwealth. GO Virginia has been funded by the general assembly since 2017 and the most recent biennial budget runs through the end of June, 2028. The position will continue as long as funding is available.

Goals Of The Position

At the direction of the Region One Council, execute strategies contained within the Growth and Diversification Plan.
Assist the Council with the “deep thinking” required to address the economic challenges facing the region.
Recommend feasible strategies that have been vetted, are supported by data, and will benefit Region One.
Coordination among constituent groups of GO Virginia including the GO Virginia State Board and the Virginia Department of Housing and Community Development
Foster relationships with local governments, educational institutions, industry partners, and economic development organizations to identify and advance GO Virginia funding opportunities.
Support collaborative planning, economic and workforce development activities, conduct economic impact analysis, review best practices and recommend projects to the Regional Council.
Develop and maintain a robust GO Virginia project pipeline by identifying, cultivating, and supporting potential projects aligned with regional economic development priorities.
Oversee the operations including accounting practices, grant administration, project management, as well as tracking and reporting of performance metrics and audit protocols.

Responsibilities And Duties

There are three categories of programmatic and administrative responsibilities for operation of the GO Virginia Program for Region One.

System Development and Strategic Planning/Execution

Manage the development and review of the Growth & Diversification Plan through stakeholder engagement, data analysis, and strategic planning
Advance strategies contained within the Growth and Diversification Plan as approved by the Regional Council
Develop and cultivate alliances and partnerships with regional stakeholders
Adhere to GO Virginia State Board and Virginia Department of Housing and Community Development guidelines

Operational and Financial

Provide staff support to regional council by coordinating regional council meetings, ensuring adherence to the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) and Conflict of Interest Act (COIA) guidelines are met
Develop and oversee the execution of an operational budget and fund management
Administer the GO Virginia Region 1 application and review process, providing technical grant assistance to prospective applicants, supporting project development, proposal refinement, and alignment with guidelines
Oversee the implementation and performance of funded projects by monitoring grant progress, ensuring compliance with grant requirements, and tracking performance metrics and outcomes
Prepare required reporting to include quarterly, annual, project monitoring reports and progress related to the Growth and Diversification Plan
Provide management support to the GO Virginia administrative team
Implement quality and continuous improvement principles and eliminate duplicative services
Identify and secure additional resources to include bridging opportunities across multiple regional councils for competitive grant funds

Communication and Outreach

Oversee the implementation of an outreach and communication strategy for the GO Virginia Region One Council to include communication tools such as newsletters, social media, marketing collateral, presentation material and the Council website
Build and maintain relationships with stakeholders including funders, employers, localities, education/workforce entities in SWVA as well as other regional councils throughout the Commonwealth
Coordinate and provide staff support for GO Virginia subcommittees focused on advancing regional GO Virginia priorities

Required Experience
: Some - up to 4 years

Significant experience building alliances and leading high impact teams, projects, and programs in a matrixed environment;
Knowledge of academic and industry environments and cultures, and ability to translate and match needs and capabilities;
Significant experience working with C-suite executives, university leaders, legislators, and government agencies to influence and impact business investment and economic development decisions;
Demonstrated experience with public-private partnerships, economic development initiatives, and pan-University initiatives.

Required Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Strong organizational and interpersonal communication skills. Excellent oral, written, presentation and facilitation skills with ability to serve as an interface between academia, industry, and government;
Ability to work collegially within a large, complex system and to negotiate with a wide range of constituencies.
Ability to project a clear message on the College’s and GO Virginia’s role in economic development with faculty, staff, students, community, corporate, and government leaders.
Ability to develop compelling value proposition statements and related materials and incorporate them into a broader communication strategy.
Ability to identify opportunities, assess situations, assemble multi-party initiatives, find mutually beneficial areas for collaboration, and communicate to all stakeholders.
Project management for complex, rapidly developing initiatives that may be ambiguous and with shifting participants.

Preferred Experience: Considerable 4-7 years

Significant experience working with senior executives, higher education leaders, and state agencies to influence and impact business investment and economic development.
Significant experience partnering with local, regional, and state economic and workforce development organizations.
Experience in managing grant funding operations.

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited four-year institution.

Preferred Education

Master’s degree in business, economics, or another related field

Additional Requirements

Required Documents

jobs.description:
Who We Are

Founded in 1965, UC Irvine
is a member of the prestigious Association of American Universities and is ranked among the nation’s top 10 public universities by U.S. News & World Report. The campus has produced five Nobel laureates and is known for its academic achievement, premier research, innovation and anteater mascot. Led by Chancellor Howard Gillman, UC Irvine has more than 36,000 students and offers 224 degree programs. It’s located in one of the world’s safest and most economically vibrant communities and is Orange County’s second-largest employer, contributing $7 billion annually to the local economy and $8 billion statewide.

To learn more about UC Irvine, visit www.uci.edu.

The School of Physical Sciences at UC Irvine hosts four nationally-ranked departments -- Chemistry, Earth System Science, Mathematics, and Physics and Astronomy — each delivering world class education and fundamental research that tangibly improves the world.We are home to the first department in the country dedicated to understanding the earth system and climate change.We have produced multiple Nobel-Prize-winning discoveries, including the realization that CfCs deplete ozone and the first detection of the neutrino, a fundamental particle of nature. Our alumni include a Nobel Laureate in chemistry, CEOs top companies, scientists finding solutions for a clean-energy economy, and innovators developing new drugs to save lives. Our faculty are working on some of the most important problems of our age, including the development of sustainable clean energy solutions, predicting cancer tumor growth with mathematics, and exploring the universe with the most powerful telescopes ever built. With an annual budget in excess of $100M, the School of Physical Sciences is an engine of innovation for the region and the globe.https://ps.uci.edu

Your Role on the Team

The School of Physical Sciences seeks a Director of Communications and External Relations. The position is a member of the senior management team and is responsible for organizational strategic direction, planning and implementation related to internal and external marketing and communications for the School, including but not limited to executive communications, alumni communications, public and media relations, community relations, and event engagement. Develops, executes, and oversees a comprehensive marketing and communications program for the school, requiring a wide variety of communications media, including written, visual, digital and electronic, and associated technical applications. Determines appropriate strategies for reaching communications and external relations goals, researches, identifies, writes, edits news releases/advisories, places university faculty in the media, solicits media, develops and manages publication production, and web development. Writes messages, written reports, and other materials to be used by School faculty and administrators in presentations to a variety of constituents in School publications, and other venues as appropriate. Maintains close liaison to the University Communications office, and works directly with the Dean and School management to develop and execute organizational communication and market branding strategy. Represents the School to the campus and community on all matters related to external relations, marketing and communications matters. The Director of External Relations plays a key strategic role in establishing the perception and visibility of the school. The position is responsible for the consistency of School materials and messages, and is critical for designing, developing, and implementing marketing and communications strategies to develop and continuously improve the reputation/brand of the School of Physical Sciences and its influence within campus wide operations. The position is directly responsible for the supervision of 2.0 FTE and has budget authority to support marketing and communications operations and activities. This position is eligible for hybrid work on a schedule that meets the business needs of leadership and the unit.

Content Production: Produces a variety of communication pieces in a variety of venues including written, visual, digital, and electronic communications. Conceptualizes, designs, writes, and distributes school's newsletter. Oversees and writes press releases, feature stories, and media advisories as well as print and electronic communication used to promote school accomplishments and activities to university audiences, external media, and community constituents. Prepares remarks and speaking materials for the Dean, as needed, and at times in collaboration with the Director of Development. Responsible for graphic design of publication projects and photo work (either shooting photos or scheduling conceptual photo shoots with campus photographer). Identifies and works with key contacts and builds and maintains relationships with university offices to achieve wider reach for school-focused content and presence. Coordinates and serves as subject matter expert for school-level marketing and communications materials. Attends monthly strategic communications meetings, represents the school on the university communications strategic management team. 25%
Strategy Implementation: Manages complex comprehensive internal and external marketing and communications efforts and activities, including written, visual, digital, and electronic communications, for the School of Physical Sciences. Works with departmental, school and campus administration to create, develop, and implement comprehensive long- and short-term strategic marketing and communications plans. Develops, executes, and oversees established objectives for the school’s internal and external marketing and communications, including the design, development, and implementation of strategies in line with the Dean’s vision. Coordinates and serves as the key contact point for internal and external school-level marketing communications materials. Provides advice and counsel to all levels of School leadership, faculty, staff, and administration on all aspects of marketing and communications, including effective messaging and problem resolution. Works with dean and faculty to produce opinion and thought pieces geared to generating an impact (increased visibility among key audiences, increased funding). Positions faculty experts when news is breaking or developing about relevant subjects. Design and implement community events and partnerships that further the dean’s vision and goals. 20%
Team Leadership: Independently supervises staff working to support scientific writing, event coordination and outreach assigns daily duties and long-term strategic priorities; performs constructive employment evaluations biannually; provides learning opportunities for career growth; responsible for recruitment and selection process when positions become vacant. Directs budget activities for the office, including review, analysis, and decision making on budget requests; and developing sound fiscal practices, plans, and strategies to deploy financial resources. As needed, solicits external vendors for print, design and/or photography requiring RFP and invoice processing. 15%

new_jobs.title: Deputy Director of External Affairs
new_jobs.description:
At the MBTA, we envision a thriving region enabled by a best-in-class transit system. Our mission is to serve the public by providing safe, reliable, and accessible transportation. MBTA’s core values are built around safety, service, equity, sustainability, culture, and accessibility, and each employee that works for the MBTA performs their roles based on our vision, mission, and values. This includes attendance, participation, and contribution in local safety committee meetings as needed.

Job Summary

The Deputy Director of External Engagement and Intergovernmental Affairs is responsible for developing and executing the External Affairs department’s public affairs strategy. In this capacity, this individual provides advice, insight, analysis, coordination, and acts as a liaison between the Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority (MBTA) and various government and regional stakeholders.

The Deputy Director is tasked with overseeing and managing the External Affairs department’s government affairs and external engagement strategies. As a leader on the External Affairs team, this person is responsible for serving as a liaison to many of the governmental agencies, partners, and service providers with which the Authority maintains relationships. Advises senior leadership on possible strategies for effectively managing governmental and interjurisdictional relationships for the benefit of the Authority's interests. Maintains constant vigilance on how the plans and activities of the Authority may interact with other stakeholder interests, and how external initiatives may impact the Authority. This position may also act as the department lead on various projects and programs that require coordination with cross-functional MBTA staff, consultants, and external organizations.

Duties & Responsibilities

Directs the operations of the Authority’s government affairs strategy by developing and advancing the MBTA’s legislative agenda in conjunction with other department leaders.
Works with department Leads and Senior Leadership in identifying and solving problems with governmental entities and/or introducing opportunities to promote the MBTA's reputation.
Represents the MBTA's interests with various government agencies, and state and local elected officials.
Acts as primary point of contact for state and local officials regarding issues related to any MBTA matter, including operations and capital projects.
Works with the Director of Capital and Community Relations to advise on and set strategic external engagement objectives related to capital projects.
Sets direction on capital project engagement related to government stakeholders.
Facilitates external communications, organizes meetings and materials, and maintains internal records.
Supports department management with drafting and submitting statutorily required legislative reports.
Assists colleagues on the External Affairs team with constituent requests.
Assists with the development and execution of outreach plans and external engagement strategies related to MBTA service, projects, and initiatives.
Monitors state legislation, analyzes legislative proposals, and provides updates and recommendations for the Assistant General Manager for External Affairs.
Maintain updated contact lists of regional stakeholders, elected officials, and staff.
Support the management and delivery of effective, timely completion of departmental and functional key initiatives, programs, and policies.
Works closely with the Office of Communications, Customer Experience, and other external-facing departments to ensure effective and proactive communication on a range of MBTA projects and events.
Attends external events as directed.
Handle all sensitive information in a strictly confidential manner.

Supervision

Will supervise Manager of Intergovernmental Affairs

applications

, whichever comes first.

Minimum Requirements & Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution, in Political Science, Public Policy, Public Administration, Communications or related field.
Five (5) years of full-time experience working in a legislative office, government agency, and/or advocacy organization.
Two (2) years of leadership and/or supervisory experience.
Excellent written and oral communications skills, with ability to communicate effectively across departments and functions.
Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.
Ability to support multiple assignments and stakeholders, prioritize workload for self, and coordinate with managers to meet deadlines.
Ability to organize data and excerise effective problem solving.
Ability to work effectively and collaboratively with a diverse workforce.
Have the maturity and confidence to interact with elected officials and staff.
Ability to travel to locations throughout the MBTA’s service areas.
Demonstrated interest in public transportation.
Have a satisfactory work record for the two (2) years prior to the closing date of this posting, including overall employment, job performance, discipline and safety records (infractions and/ or offenses occurring after the closing of this posting and before the filling of a vacancy may preclude a candidate from consideration for selection).

Substitutions

A High School Diploma or GED with an additional seven (7) years of directly related experience substitutes for the bachelor’s degree requirement.
An associate’s degree from an accredited institution and an additional three (3) years of directly related experience substitutes for the bachelor’s degree requirement.
A master’s degree in a related subject substitutes for two (2) years of general experience.
A nationally recognized certification, or statewide/professional certification in a related field substitutes for one year of experience.

Preferred Experience & Skills

Master's degree from an accredited institution in Public Administration, Business Administration, Communications, or related degree.
Experience developing and delivering presentations to senior level executives.
Experience working in a large, matrixed organization.
Experience in local, state, or national politics/legislative affairs.

Job Conditions

Ability to effectively read, comprehend, communicate, and respond to instructions, orders, signs, notices, inquiries, etc. in English.
Be at least eighteen (18) years of age, except if participating in an approved high school internship / co-op program.
Ability to commute to assigned work locations in the Boston, MA metro area, as required by the role.
Ability to provide internal and external customers with courteous and professional experiences.
Ability to work effectively, independently, and as part of a diverse workforce team (or supervise, if required).
Ability to uphold the rights and interests of the MBTA while building and maintaining effective relationships with employees and co-workers.
Ability to adhere to rules, regulations, collective bargaining agreements (if applicable), and policies of the MBTA, including the EEO, anti-discrimination, anti-harassment, and anti-retaliation policies.
Have a satisfactory work record for the two (2) years immediately prior to the closing date of this posting (unless if current student or recent graduate), including overall employment, job performance, discipline, and safety records (infractions and/or offenses occurring after the closing of the posting and before the filling of a vacancy may preclude a candidate from consideration for selection).
Ability to pass a Criminal Offender Record Information (CORI) check, comprehensive background screening, and / or medical Clinic screening, potentially including physical examination and drug and alcohol screenings.
Ability to work all shifts and / or locations assigned, directed, or necessary for this position, including (for some transit / operations roles) up to twenty-four (24) hours per day, seven (7) days per week as necessary to accommodate severe weather conditions, emergencies, or any other circumstances that may potentially impact service or the safety of service.
Intern / co-op staff must be enrolled full or part-time in an accredited educational program and maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 2.5 for the entire duration of the internship / co-op. Additionally, interns / co-ops must have valid work authorization and U.S. Social Security Number prior to starting pre-employment screenings / pre-boarding, working in their positions, and throughout the duration of their program.
